# `silk/machine/explore`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Walks a machine through every state it can reach: [`Explorer`](#Explorer) and [`Walk`](#Walk).

## When to use
Use this module to check a machine as a whole, in a test. [`Explorer.walk`](#Explorer.impl.walk) runs the machine
for real, with its guards, its context and its regions, and gives back every step it could
take. The walk then answers questions about the whole machine: which events no state
handles, which states nothing reaches, which rows overlap, and what a command leaves from
start to end. Use the `silk.machine.paths` module for one path to each state of one chart
read as data.

## Details
The walk starts from the snapshots it is given and sends every event of a list to each
snapshot it has not seen. Two snapshots are the same when their MessagePack bytes are, so
the state union, the event union, the context and the effects must implement `Schema`. A
state that waits for the world, see `Chart.awaits`, gets only the events it waits for.
Every other state gets only the events that no state waits for.

## Gotchas
The walk ends only when the machine has a finite number of snapshots. Give
[`Explorer.walk`](#Explorer.impl.walk) a limit, and check [`Walk.complete`](#Walk.complete).

Import as `Explorer` with `import silk.machine.explore { Explorer }`.

<a id="Explorer.impl.walk"></a>

### Associated function `walk`

```silk
pub effect fn walk<S: Machine<E, C, X> + Schema, E: Schema, C: Schema, X: Schema>(
    starts: List<Snapshot<S, E, C, X>>,
    events: &[E],
    limit: usize,
  ) -> Walk<S, E, C, X>
    ! SchemaError | OutOfMemoryError | TransitionLoopError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Walks the machine from each snapshot of `starts`, sending every event of `events` to
every snapshot it reaches, until it has seen them all or holds `limit` snapshots.

#### Details
A snapshot whose active state waits for the world, see `Chart.awaits`, gets the events
of `events` that it waits for. Any other snapshot gets the events that no state of the
machine waits for. A machine that is done, stopped or failed gets none. The effects a
step queued are moved into its [`Step`](#Step), so every snapshot of the walk has none pending.

#### Errors
`SchemaError` when a snapshot or an event cannot be written as MessagePack or read back.
`TransitionLoopError` when a step never settles. `OutOfMemoryError`.

Returns the positions in [`Walk.steps`](#Walk.steps) of the steps that no state handled, in the order
the walk took them. Each one is a state and an event that nobody wrote a row for.


Returns the positions in [`Walk.nodes`](#Walk.nodes) of the snapshots that can take no event: the

<a id="Walk.impl.runs"></a>

### Method `runs`

```silk
pub effect fn runs(self: &Self, limit: usize) -> List<Run>
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns every run of the walk: for each step from a snapshot that waits for nothing, the
step and each way the world can answer until the machine waits for nothing again.

#### Details
A step that reaches a snapshot that waits for the world continues with each step from
that snapshot, so one event gives one run for each combination of answers. A run stops
after `limit` steps with [`Run.settled`](#Run.settled) false, which is how a machine whose answers
go in a circle shows. Steps that no state handled start no run.
